purpose: Coverage inventory for the EUROMOD Belgium BE_2025 model surface against Belgium RuleSpec. EUROMOD is an executable comparison oracle, not legal authority; statutory and regulatory RuleSpec modules must still cite upstream Belgian law.
coverage_claim: Current Axiom coverage has twenty-two EUROMOD-facing output concepts: gross employee SSC tscee_s is live-verified for the regular worker statutory slice; employee work-bonus reduction tsceerd_s and derived net SSC tscee_net_s run live with Belgium-specific synthetic labour inputs and expose a narrow 2025 timing residual; employer SSC tscer_s live-compares ordinary private-sector commercial employer cases and exposes EUROMOD issue #11 because BE_2025 uses stale company-closing-fund rates relative to the official ONSS 2025 FFE workbook; PIT tin_s has a composed single-worker pilot that nets ordinary employee SSC before Article 51 forfait expenses, applies the Article 5/2 autonomy factor, computes Article 289ter/1 work-bonus credit amounts from encoded ONSS full-year equal-month work-bonus A/B amounts capped by personal contributions actually granted, treats the Article 289ter/1 credit as refundable under CIR 92 Articles 290 and 304, and live-compares 10k, 30k, and 60k full-year equal-month worker cases: 30k and 60k match, while 10k exposes EUROMOD issue #12 because BE_2025 uses uncapped A/B credit bases; the household tax income-list aggregate ils_tax live-verifies a narrow worker-PIT pilot for the 30k and 60k worker cases, while capital-income-tax and property-tax composition remain open; self-employed social contributions tscse_s live-verifies for main-activity floor, first-bracket, high-income, and capped cases after bridging EUROMOD's uprated yse into Axiom, and exposes filed EUROMOD threshold-allowance residuals for secondary and post-pension cases; special social-security contribution tsceesp_s bridges EUROMOD's returned il_taxabley base into the Article 108 household contribution and live-verifies the low and middle single-worker statutory slice while exposing a filed EUROMOD Article 108 schedule issue for high-income single and joint-assessment cases; Flemish care/social-protection premium tci_s is live-verified for ordinary and reduced-premium adult Flanders cases using Article 68 plus official Statbel health-index values; Flemish jobbonus bwkrg_s is live-compared for seven worker cases: a matching Brussels non-resident zero case, a matching tiny part-time suppression case, and five visible full-time/half-time residuals tracked as EUROMOD issue #10 because BE_2025 uses older jobbonus thresholds, a 600 EUR maximum, and no 2025 fixed top-up; indexed cadastral income khooo_s live-compares CIR 92 Article 518 indexation and exposes EUROMOD issue #14 because BE_2025 tprhm_be leaves the indexed cadastral-income product unrounded; immovable withholding tprhm_s is live-verified for high-cadastral-income no-reduction Flanders, Brussels, and Wallonia cases after bridging EUROMOD's returned annual khooo_s into Axiom and using supplied local centimes; maternity leave bmact_s live-verifies the ordinary employed mother/newborn household slice, including an under-cap path and a high-wage Article 113 cap path, with EUROMOD extension switch PBE=on, mapping the encoded Article 216 first-30-day 82 percent and after-30-day 75 percent rest-period amount to EUROMOD after bridging annualized yem into uncapped daily remuneration as yem / 312 and supplying the BE_2025 Article 113 cap input for the capped case; birth-leave bpact_s live-verifies the father/newborn household slice, including an under-cap path and a high-wage Article 87 cap path, with the same PBE switch and yem / 312 bridge plus supplied BE_2025 Article 87 cap input; regional birth allowance bchba_s is live-verified for Brussels first/multiple and later-child amounts, Flanders first/later amounts, and Wallonia first/later amounts, while the German-speaking Community newborn case exposes EUROMOD issue #13 because BE_2025 bchba_be returns zero for drgn1=4; monthly child benefit bch_s live-verifies for a one-child high-income base-amount slice in Brussels, Flanders, and Wallonia across age and higher-education branches, and live-compares German-speaking Community base cases that expose EUROMOD issue #8 because BE_2025 bch_be returns zero for drgn1=4, plus one-child social-supplement slices for Brussels Article 9 low-income cases covering ages 0, 13, and 18 higher education, same-age Brussels Article 9 household aggregates covering two- and three-child low-income and middle-income cases, and Wallonia new-system Article 13 low- and middle-income age-0 cases, while pre-2020 Wallonia social-supplement cases expose filed EUROMOD transition issue #9; social-integration income support bsa_s live-verifies for isolated adult and single-parent dependent-child no-resources cases using the 2025 current monthly amount bridge; elderly income guarantee bsaoa_s live-verifies for an isolated no-resources senior when the BE_2025 bsaoa_be policy is temporarily switched on in the EUROMOD model XML overlay; the household benefit income-list aggregate ils_ben live-verifies a narrow family-benefit pilot that composes birth allowance and child benefit for four Brussels, Flanders, and Wallonia household cases, while broader benefit-list composition remains open; and the household disposable-income aggregate ils_dispy live-verifies a narrow worker PIT/SIC pilot for 30k and 55k single-worker cases by composing original employment income, the worker PIT pilot, ordinary employee SSC, and the Article 108 special social-security contribution, while full disposable-income composition remains open. The broader BE_2025 model has 43 policy nodes and is not yet covered end-to-end.

oracle_configuration.configuration_note: Live synthetic comparisons use the BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 dataset configuration and BE_training_data as the template dataset so EUROMOD's Belgian uprating and policy switches run while synthetic rows retain the training schema.

denominator.unit: EUROMOD BE_2025 policy/function nodes parsed from BE.xml

coverage_summary.rule_percentage_note: No percentage is reported until each BE_2025 policy/function is mapped to RuleSpec modules and marked encoded, composed, oracle-tested, or gap.

oracle_output_coverage.meaning: gross employee social contributions before work-bonus reduction
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: The RuleSpec Article 38 before-reductions bridge and the axiom-oracles EUROMOD Belgium live comparison both compute tscee_s as 13.07 percent of EUROMOD gross yem for the 30k and 60k single-worker cases.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Full ONSS contribution bases, special regimes, and household integration remain partial.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: The live 30k single-worker comparison bridges EUROMOD yemeq_s into RuleSpec's supplied annual work-bonus reference remuneration. EUROMOD returns 3398.52 while RuleSpec returns 3386.87 because EUROMOD applies the February-onward 2025 work-bonus table to all 12 months and RuleSpec weights January separately from February through December.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Partial-year, part-time, manual-worker, and future month-varying work-bonus mechanics are not yet encoded; the January-vs-February 2025 timing difference is intentionally visible instead of hidden by tolerance.

oracle_output_coverage.meaning: derived oracle output tscee_s minus tsceerd_s
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: The oracle adapter derives tscee_net_s from EUROMOD tscee_s and tsceerd_s so the Axiom after-work-bonus contribution is compared to the same household-level quantity. The 30k residual is -11.65, exactly the inverse of the work-bonus timing residual.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Depends on the work-bonus residual and broader special-regime coverage.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec encodes the ONSS DmfA 2025 Q1 ordinary employer bridge for private-sector commercial employers from the 19.88 percent basic tax-shift rate, the 4.27 percent wage-moderation formula on remuneration and the basic employer contribution, the 1.69 percent 1.60-contribution including wage moderation, and the official ONSS 2025 FFE workbook parenthesized less-than-20-worker rate of 0.18 percent. The 2026-07-04 live comparison bridges EUROMOD's returned annual yem into Axiom and shows EUROMOD tscer_s at exactly 26.75 percent of gross for both 30k and 60k worker cases, while Axiom returns the source-backed 26.868876 percent path. The residual is filed upstream as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#11 because BE_2025 uses 0.06 percent and 0.12 percent company-closing-fund rates instead of the official ONSS 2025 workbook's 0.18 percent and 0.23 percent rates including wage moderation.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Exact EUROMOD parity is blocked by the filed employer-SSC parameter issue rather than an Axiom statutory encoding gap. Broader employer-contribution parity still needs special employer categories, structural reductions, manual-worker vacation contributions, at-least-20-worker cases, and full household contribution bases.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec encodes Royal Decree No. 38 Article 12 self-employed contribution rates, including the statutory 20.50 percent first-bracket rate and 14.16 percent second-bracket rate, and Article 13 pension-age rates. axiom-oracles maps the selected annual contribution to EUROMOD tscse_s, bridges EUROMOD's returned annual yse into Axiom gross income, and uses the BE_2025 Article 14 factor implied by EUROMOD's current Article 12 threshold. The 2026-07-03 live comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches all four main-activity cases: 5k floor, 30k first bracket, 60k high first bracket, and 120k capped/second-bracket case. The same report intentionally shows three residuals for secondary and post-pension cases because EUROMOD treats the Article 12 section 2 and Article 13 section 1 thresholds as deductible allowances; that model issue is filed upstream as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#6 and tracked in euromod_issues.json.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Broader self-employed SSC parity still needs student, spouse-helper, starter, survivor-pension, prior-year-income, and expense/loss cases. Secondary activity and post-pension cases are encoded and oracle-exercised, but exact EUROMOD parity is blocked by the filed threshold-allowance issue rather than an Axiom statutory encoding gap.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec encodes Law of 30 March 1994 Article 108's annual household special social-security contribution schedule and maps it to EUROMOD tsceesp_s. The oracle suite bridges EUROMOD's returned annual il_taxabley into RuleSpec's Article 107 household-income input. The 2026-07-04 live comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches 3/7 cases: the 10k zero case, the 30k single-worker middle-band case, and the 55k single-worker fourth-band case within the 1 EUR tolerance. The 80k single-worker case and all three joint-assessment cases intentionally show residuals tracked as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#7: EUROMOD's BE_2025 tsceesp_be schedule uses misstated single thresholds/cap behavior and appears to swap the joint 1.3 percent band with the plateau band.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Broader special-contribution parity still needs Article 107 income construction from full PIT variables, Article 109 payroll withholding comparisons, Article 110 settlement/refund comparisons, treaty exclusions, special worker categories, and resolution of the filed EUROMOD Article 108 schedule issue.

oracle_output_coverage.meaning: Flemish care insurance / social protection contribution
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec computes the 2025 Flemish Social Protection ordinary and reduced annual premiums from Article 68: 54 EUR and 27 EUR base amounts multiplied by the official Statbel April 2024 / April 2020 health-index ratio on base year 2013 and rounded to the nearest euro, yielding 64 EUR and 32 EUR. axiom-oracles maps the annual premium to EUROMOD tci_s and adds BE_2025 adult Flanders cases with drgn1=2: a high-income ordinary adult with brv_s=0 and a reduced-premium adult whose bsa input triggers EUROMOD brv_s>0. The 2026-07-03 live comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data returns EUROMOD tci_s = 64.00 and 32.00, matching Axiom exactly.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Broader Flemish Social Protection parity still needs voluntary Brussels affiliation, administrative affiliation without premium, arrears, and sanctions.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec encodes the Flemish Codex decree of 20 May 2022 and the Flemish Government implementing order consolidated as of 1 January 2025: lower monthly gross threshold 2,115 EUR, upper threshold 3,114.99 EUR, maximum full-time annual base 650 EUR, degressive floor 50 EUR, 50 EUR fixed top-up when payable, and 50/10 EUR full-time/part-time small-payment thresholds. The 2026-07-04 live axiom-oracles comparison maps this output to EUROMOD bwkrg_s, bridges EUROMOD yemeq_s into Axiom monthly gross, and runs five full-time worker cases plus two part-time probes. The Brussels non-Flanders case and tiny part-time suppression case match at zero; the four Flanders full-time worker cases and one low-wage half-time worker case intentionally show residuals of 100.00, 100.00, 168.9985, 168.9952, and 75.00 EUR because EUROMOD BE_2025 bwkrg_be uses 1,800/2,500 EUR wage thresholds, a 600 EUR maximum, a 20 EUR full-time suppression threshold, and no 2025 fixed top-up. This is filed upstream as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#10.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Broader part-time and partial-year jobbonus cases, frontier workers, administrative payroll reconstruction, and resolution of the filed EUROMOD stale-parameter issue remain outside exact parity.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec encodes CIR 92 Article 518 cadastral-income indexation from the current FisconetPlus consolidated statute and official SPF Finances annual coefficients, including nearest-euro rounding after applying the 2025 coefficient 2.2446. The 2026-07-04 live BE_2025 synthetic comparison maps that output to EUROMOD khooo_s and runs two property-owner cases. The 5000 EUR non-indexed cadastral-income exact-multiple case matches at 11223 EUR; the 1000 EUR case intentionally shows EUROMOD khooo_s = 2244.6000000000004 against Axiom 2245 because BE_2025 tprhm_be computes khooo_s as khooo * $khooo_uprate without the Article 518 nearest-euro rounding step. That residual is filed upstream as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#14.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Exact indexed cadastral-income parity is blocked by filed upstream EUROMOD issue #14. Broader cadastral-income parity still needs cadastral-income establishment, reassessment, Article 15 proportional reductions, regional reductions, and household/property ownership allocation.

oracle_output_coverage.meaning: immovable withholding / advance levy on immovable property
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec composes the ordinary Belgium/Flanders regional rates with supplied provincial, agglomeration, and communal additional centimes, routes Flanders, Brussels, and Wallonia with a supplied region input, and maps gross tax after supplied local centimes to EUROMOD tprhm_s. The 2026-07-04 live BE_2025 comparison bridges EUROMOD's returned annual khooo_s cadastral-income base into Axiom and matches all three high-cadastral-income no-reduction cases exactly: Flanders, Brussels, and Wallonia.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Broader immovable-withholding parity still needs cadastral-income determination, Article 518 rounding once EUROMOD issue #14 is resolved, reductions, remissions, exemptions including BE HOME, provincial/agglomeration/communal centime table ingestion, low-income thresholds, taxpayer aggregation, and other property-tax cases. EUROMOD raw khooo_s and tprhm_s are already annual-law amounts and are intentionally not annualized by the adapter.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec maps Brussels, Flanders, Wallonia, and the German-speaking Community 2025 birth-allowance amounts to EUROMOD bchba_s using upstream regional/community statutes for entitlement plus official 2025 amount surfaces for indexed amounts. The live BE_2025 synthetic comparison covers Brussels first/multiple birth 1367.74 EUR, Brussels later child 621.70 EUR, Flanders first/later child 1238.78 EUR, Wallonia first/later child 1367.74 EUR, and a German-speaking Community newborn birth premium of 1376.16 EUR. Brussels, Flanders, and Wallonia match exactly; the German-speaking Community case intentionally shows EUROMOD bchba_s = 0 against Axiom 1376.16 because BE_2025 bchba_be has no visible drgn1=4 branch. That residual is filed upstream as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#13.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Exact German-speaking Community birth-allowance parity is blocked by the filed EUROMOD bchba_be region-scope issue rather than an Axiom statutory encoding gap. Broader family-benefit parity still needs allocation/payment-recipient rules, multiple-birth edge cases beyond the current one-child birth component, statutory payment timing, and expansion of ils_ben beyond the family-benefit pilot.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec computes 2025 annualized base child-benefit amounts for a one-child, high-income household slice in Brussels, Flanders, Wallonia, and the German-speaking Community, the Brussels Article 9 one-child low-income social supplement and same-age household aggregate branch from upstream Brussels statutory/official amount-table sources, the Wallonia Article 13 one-child new-system social supplement from the Walloon decree plus official AVIQ indexed amount tables, and the Wallonia pre-2020 LGAF low-income transition path from Walloon Articles 120, 123, and 128. axiom-oracles maps those annual amounts to EUROMOD bch_s, uses explicit education-code projection dec=6 for higher-education branches, and bridges EUROMOD il_bch_means into the Article 9 income input for the Brussels same-age household aggregate suite. The 2026-07-04 live BE_2025 synthetic comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches 13/17 base cases, 3/3 Brussels one-child social-supplement cases, 4/4 Brussels same-age household aggregate cases, and 2/8 Wallonia social-supplement cases exactly. The four German-speaking Community base residuals are tracked as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#8 because EUROMOD returns zero for drgn1=4, while RuleSpec returns the statutory 157 EUR monthly base plus the 62.55 EUR 2025 annual supplement. The six pre-2020 Wallonia social-supplement residuals are tracked as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#9 because EUROMOD appears to add the decree Article 13 supplement to children that remain under the LGAF transition path. The BE family-benefit oracle sets EUROMOD byr to zero because BE_2025 treats byr as early-retirement pension income, not birth year.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Exact German-speaking Community child-benefit parity is blocked by filed upstream EUROMOD issue #8, and exact Wallonia pre-2020 social-supplement parity is blocked by filed upstream EUROMOD issue #9. Broader child-benefit parity still needs low-income/social supplement branches beyond the Brussels Article 9 same-age and Wallonia Article 13 one-child slices, orphan/disability/single-parent supplements, mixed-age multiple-child rank/composition mechanics, allocation/payment-recipient rules, and expansion of ils_ben beyond the family-benefit pilot.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec has a dense-executable worker-remuneration-to-PIT pipeline that composes Article 38 ordinary employee SSC into the PIT professional-income base, then applies Article 51 forfait expenses, Article 130/134 tax, the Article 5/2 autonomy factor, Article 289ter/1 work-bonus credit amounts computed from encoded ONSS full-year equal-month A/B work-bonus amounts capped by employee contributions actually granted, refundable Article 289ter/1 imputation under CIR 92 Articles 290 and 304, and supplied local rates. The 2026-07-04 live synthetic comparison matches the 30k and 60k worker cases within the 15 EUR tolerance. The 10k low-wage refundable-credit case intentionally remains a visible residual: EUROMOD tin_s is -1504.8488879999998 while Axiom returns -724.4815561100447, a -780.367331889955 difference tracked as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#12 because BE_2025 computes the PIT credit from uncapped i_tsceerdA_s/i_tsceerdB_s instead of the actually granted capped reduction amounts.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: This is single-worker PIT pilot comparison, not full household PIT. Exact low-wage PIT parity is blocked by filed EUROMOD issue #12 unless upstream confirms the uncapped interpretation; full parity also needs joint assessment, dependants, other income categories, regional reductions, withholding tables, local rate ingestion, and final imputation ordering outside the pilot.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec exposes a dense-executable social-integration income-support output that composes Article 3/4 eligibility, Article 14/15 selected amounts, supplied Chapter II resources, and cent-presented monthly support into an annual amount. axiom-oracles maps that concept to EUROMOD bsa_s and supplies the official 2025 monthly category amounts used by the BE_2025 model. The 2026-07-04 live comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches both cases exactly: isolated adult no resources at 15770.40 EUR/year and single parent with one dependent child/no resources at 21312.84 EUR/year.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Broader social-assistance parity still needs itemized resources, cohabitant resources, earned-income disregards in live cases, CPAS equity/procedure surfaces, and additional household composition variants.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec now exposes a dense-executable GRAPA annual output that composes Article 6 selected maximum amount, Article 7 resources, and Article 11 resource reduction. axiom-oracles maps that concept to EUROMOD bsaoa_s and adds a BE_2025 isolated-senior no-resources suite case using EUROMOD's 2025 current monthly Cat2 amount, 1,580.37 EUR, as a supplied current-amount bridge. The 2026-07-03 live comparison temporarily patches the BE_2025 bsaoa_be policy switch on in a model XML overlay and returns EUROMOD bsaoa_s = 18,964.44 and Axiom belgium_grapa_income_guarantee_for_elderly_annual_amount = 18,964.44.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Broader GRAPA parity still needs current-amount source ingestion, detailed delegated resource exclusions, property and capital resource calculations, cohabiting cases, and administrative eligibility surfaces.

oracle_output_coverage.meaning: ordinary unemployment benefit (PART SIMULATED; bun_be switched on per run)
oracle_output_coverage.note: bun_be ships off (PART SIMULATED); switched on via euromod_policy_switch_overrides. EUROMOD bun_s = 0.65 x min(post-uprating prior monthly wage, 3432.38 EUR/month) for the ordinary first spell month (stored /12; bridge annualises x12). The composed RuleSpec pilot returns the RD 25.11.1991 Article 111 A1 daily-cap-bound monthly payable. Four first-month single cases: all dispositioned upstream_engine_gap (EUROMOD stylised monthly highwage cap vs statutory Article 111 daily cap A1, no Article 115 floor, no Article 114 degressivity).

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec encodes Royal Decree of 3 July 1996 Article 216 ordinary maternity indemnity rates: 82 percent of uncapped daily remuneration for the first 30 working days for Article 86 item 1 a/b workers and 75 percent of Article 113-capped daily remuneration after day 30. axiom-oracles adds BE_2025 mother/newborn household cases, enables EUROMOD extension switch PBE=on for bmact_be, and bridges EUROMOD's returned annualized yem to Axiom uncapped daily remuneration as yem / 312. Under-cap cases bridge the same daily amount into the Article 113-capped input; the high-wage case keeps the capped daily input supplied at the BE_2025 Article 113 daily cap of 183.13 while bridging only uncapped daily remuneration. The 2026-07-05 live comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches the 30k, 45k, and 60k employed mother/newborn cases exactly after EUROMOD uprating.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Maternity eligibility and waiting-stage reconstruction, unemployment and self-employed maternity branches, protection-period scheduling, multiple-birth and hospitalization extensions, payment allocation, and upstream ingestion of the indexed Article 113 cap source remain supplied or outside the verified slice.

oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec encodes Law of 3 July 1978 Article 30 first three employer-paid days plus Royal Decree of 3 July 1996 Article 223bis at 82 percent for the final seventeen days. axiom-oracles adds BE_2025 father/newborn household cases, enables EUROMOD extension switch PBE=on for the bpact_be policy, and bridges EUROMOD's returned annualized yem to Axiom uncapped daily remuneration as yem / 312. Under-cap cases bridge the same daily amount into the Article 87-capped input; the high-wage case keeps the capped daily input supplied at the BE_2025 daily cap of 183.13 while bridging only uncapped daily remuneration. The 2026-07-05 live comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches the 30k, 45k, and 60k father/newborn cases exactly after EUROMOD uprating.
oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Eligibility/filiation/cohabitation reconstruction, working-history gates, allocation, leave scheduling, and upstream ingestion of the indexed Article 87 cap source remain supplied or outside the verified slice. Broader parental leave, incapacity, and disability parity remain open.

This is not full tax-list parity. Broader ils_tax coverage still needs capital-income tax, immovable withholding and other wealth/property tax composition, joint assessment, regional/local reductions, and non-worker income categories. Social contributions remain outside ils_tax in EUROMOD and feed disposable income through ils_sicdy.
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec composes the encoded worker PIT pilot into a narrow EUROMOD ils_tax worker-PIT aggregate with supplied zero capital-income-tax and property-tax components. The live BE_2025 synthetic comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches the 30k and 60k worker cases within the statutory PIT oracle tolerance. The 10k low-wage case remains excluded from the exact ils_tax pilot because the underlying tin_s residual is tracked as ec-jrc/JRC-EUROMOD-software-source-code#12.

oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: This is not full benefit-list parity. Broader ils_ben coverage still needs social assistance, GRAPA, unemployment, pensions, disability, leave, jobbonus and other regional/community benefits, payment-recipient allocation, multi-newborn birth-premium aggregation, and composition with benefit interactions beyond the current no-other-benefits family slice.
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec composes encoded household birth-allowance and child-benefit outputs into a narrow EUROMOD ils_ben family-benefit pilot aggregate. The 2026-07-05 live BE_2025 synthetic comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches 4/4 high- or middle-income family-benefit cases exactly: Brussels age-0 child benefit plus birth allowance, Flanders age-13 child benefit, Wallonia age-0 child benefit plus birth allowance, and Brussels two same-age age-13 children with the Article 9 middle-income supplement. The first probe showed EUROMOD includes bchba_s in ils_ben for age-0 children, so the Axiom aggregate includes the birth component for one-child age-0 cases.

oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: This is not full disposable-income parity. Broader ils_dispy coverage still needs complete original-income construction, full benefit-list and tax-list composition, self-employed and pensioner social contributions, joint assessment, non-worker income categories, payment-recipient allocation, and household-level interaction ordering.
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: RuleSpec composes a narrow EUROMOD ils_dispy worker PIT/SIC aggregate as original employment income plus supplied benefits minus the encoded worker PIT pilot, ordinary employee social-security contribution, Article 108 special social-security contribution, and supplied other social-insurance contributions. The live BE_2025 synthetic comparison under dataset BE_2024_c1_2015_03_e2 with template_dataset BE_training_data matches the 30k and 55k single-worker cases within the disposable-income oracle tolerance after bridging EUROMOD's returned yem, yemeq_s, and il_taxabley values into Axiom.

oracle_output_coverage.remaining_gap: Used to align comparisons on EUROMOD's own post-uprating gross; not a RuleSpec parity target.

oracle_output_coverage.meaning: study allowance (Flemish study grant and school allowance; French-Community allocation d'etudes), region-routed
oracle_output_coverage.evidence: The region-routing module selects the Flemish or French-Community study allowance by drgn1. Six single-household BE_2025 cases match bed_s exactly — in one run_cases batch as well as solo, since the adapter runs each household as its own engine run: Flanders higher-education full 3046.30 and intermediate 2092.30, Flanders secondary 1139.56, Wallonia higher-education 869.21, and Flanders and Wallonia above-threshold zeros. The Flemish study grant, Flemish school allowance, and French-Community allocation surfaces supply the routed amounts. BE_2025 also applies a seeded per-household non-take-up lottery to bed_s (active under real dataset-configuration names); per-household engine runs pin every case to the passing solo draw (see euromod_issues.json euromod-be-2025-bed-study-allowance-batch-position-contamination). Brussels' random ninety-ten community split keys on the same draw, so Brussels stays out of scope.

domain_coverage.oracle_status: tin_s worker pilot now compares live against EUROMOD after SSC netting, Article 5/2 autonomy-factor ordering, capped Article 289ter/1 work-bonus credit bases, and Article 289ter/1 refundability; 30k and 60k match, while the 10k low-wage case exposes filed EUROMOD issue #12 because BE_2025 uses uncapped work-bonus A/B bases. This is still not full household parity. ils_tax live-verifies a narrow worker-PIT pilot for 30k and 60k worker cases with supplied zero capital-income-tax and property-tax components. The narrow ils_dispy worker pilot reuses this worker-PIT component inside a disposable-income aggregate for 30k and 55k cases.
